issue: Accepted battle outcomes can produce unloadable saves
evidence: A valid turn-236 save (602413fe), followed by accepted attack and autoResolveBattle, leaves morale 59 on a unit whose base is 55; deserializeGame throws. Independently, Standard24 seed74 turn101 and B74 final252 retain battle-report morale above validator bounds although full replay is exact.
why: An ordinary successful battle can make current progress impossible to save/restore. The tested storage adapter protects the previous valid slot, but that does not save subsequent progress.
solution: Define canonical strategic morale versus battle-only bonuses; apply temporary training effects once; reconcile survivors without carrying those bonuses into future deployments; preserve and version historical battle facts. Add round-trip invariants at each accepted battle boundary, not only after End turn. Do not fix by deleting reports or weakening validation indiscriminately.
acceptance: Both retained corrupt-save symptoms become version-correct loadable states; minimal two-command red regression passes; manual/automatic/retreat/assault/same-turn repeated battles round-trip through autosave and export/import with deterministic continuation.

issue: Normal large campaigns outgrow the full-archive save format
evidence: Standard/24, Long, seed748291 reaches real victory turn446 with 114244 accepted orders and 1496 recorded battles. State snapshot is 10912745 bytes, but serializeCampaign fails with Save exceeds the 64 MiB limit.
why: A supported campaign can become impossible to save/export or finish its promised chronicle workflow even though the current state is modest.
solution: Separate bounded transactional playable-state saves from append-only/chunked campaign history and optional battle presentation records. Use real quota accounting, atomic manifest/checkpoint updates, size warnings and recoverable export. Preserve coverage flags and truthful partial-history handling; do not silently drop history or merely raise the input limit.
acceptance: The retained Standard24/Long archive exports, imports and restores exact state/history within a documented browser memory/quota budget; interruption and quota-exhaustion tests preserve the previous valid save.

issue: Twenty-one co-located formations make a legal force unattackable
evidence: A fresh generated paid-muster scenario reaches 21 scout formations by turn52. Save-valid field probes reject 21 defenders and accept 20. A 21-guard garrison remains at 1260 strength after ten siege turns and cannot be assaulted even at zero defenses/supplies.
why: Ordinary recruiting can create invulnerable capitals or victory hosts. Army-container limits do not prevent co-located-stack immunity.
solution: Implement bounded participants plus explicit reserves/reinforcement, or another deliberate legal stacking policy, with no troop deletion and a contestable route through every valid defending stack. Give the UI and AI the same participation preview.
acceptance: Earned and authored 20/21/larger field, town and fleet cases remain attackable/assaultable and save-compatible; large resolution stays within the battle budget.

issue: Extended campaign length substitutes accumulation for late strategic development
evidence: D Tiny4 Epic seed99 ends turn808; all practical trees complete by146, last battle/capture297, winning project starts748. From300 through808 one tracked army uses only two cells. The final knowledge stock is 172421 with no further practical nodes.
why: Hundreds of extra turns create time cost, not hundreds of turns of adaptation or payoff.
solution: Define early/middle/endgame decision-density and pressure goals per pace; couple escalation to new strategic opportunities, rival threats and public projects. Recalibrate price/window scaling only after those loops exist. Keep Short clearly a skirmish profile rather than using it to conceal Standard/Epic gaps.
acceptance: Multiple earned Standard/Long/Epic campaigns show continuing consequential choices after research saturation, measurable project contest attempts and finite non-busywork endings; publish quiet-turn and contact distributions.

issue: Only Prosperity ends campaigns; conquest and defeat lack their promised terminal models
evidence: Victory type and terminal setter only support prosperity. All seven completed primary simulations end through that path. Current Gate B asks for at least three tested paths while the master product brief names five; neither requirement is satisfied by one exchange project.
why: Different strategies still converge on financing the same project, and destroying every rival is not an independently implemented ending.
solution: Implement the agreed release path set with distinct progress, warnings, counterplay and clear defeat/elimination. Do not silently lower the five-path product target to the three-path minimum gate; explicitly ratify any smaller non-filler scope before implementation.
acceptance: Each retained release path is won and lost through ordinary generated campaigns, can be disrupted, communicates progress and survives save/replay; elimination never leaves a dead player pressing End turn indefinitely.

issue: Strategic AI lacks durable plans for contact, war and project counterplay
evidence: Unchanged Standard/4-seat contact test fails its 100-turn expectation; actual Ashen contact appears at137 in D sparse. Epic army.145 has 720 A-B-A returns and exact158↔159 movement late. AI does expand, research, transport, fight and win; legality is not the defect.
why: Large geography and late victory threats fail to produce consistently purposeful opposition.
solution: Retain observation-only legal planners and existing enemy-project target awareness; add bounded saved objectives/theater commitments, route progress and loop detection so those intentions become executed operations. Introduce disclosed difficulty policy separately from pace. Keep the original contact threshold unless a justified design change is explicitly adopted.
acceptance: Existing contact gate passes honestly; trajectory tests distinguish useful patrol from fruitless reversals; multiple factions assemble and execute attacks on exposed project hosts through land and sea without hidden information.

issue: The attention system misses unused workers and economic danger
evidence: Campaign A turn9: population3 with 0/3 workers; turn26: First Ember3/5. Next-action navigation only considers movable armies and empty production queues.
why: New players silently underperform; experienced players must repeatedly inspect every settlement as the empire grows.
solution: Add categorized attention entries for unassigned households, forecast deficits, interrupted work/routes and urgent threats, each with consequence and locate/action. Offer explicit assignment policies with manually locked tiles. Build the same summary into a sortable empire table.
acceptance: A growing town with a full queue still reports new unused labor; two/ten/forty-town scenarios can resolve attention without reopening every modal; forecasts match simulation.

issue: Twenty-four cultures share most decisive rules and access
evidence: 24 culture definitions, 19 AI recruitment-weight vectors, but all 13 units, their prices/prerequisites, ten technologies, identical Flame1/Rune1 casters and victory rules are shared. Ecological affinities and cultivation differences are real.
why: Choosing another people changes optimization and presentation more than the strategy available, below the stated replayability bar.
solution: Prove a small contrast cohort before expanding every culture: each needs an economic constraint, military/magical opportunity, progression identity and adversarial counter. Use data-driven capabilities and the existing lore rather than faction engine forks or renamed stat copies.
acceptance: Blind comparison of two contrasting factions changes opening decisions, army/resource priorities and at least one late plan; AI understands each exception; no extra faction is counted complete on artwork alone.

issue: Magic is two universal battle spells, not a strategic pillar
evidence: C99 paid for both discoveries and a real caster; battle.80 turn37 contains actual Cinder thread/Bound ward casts and strain10. Catalog/state contain no rituals, summons, items/recipes, sacred/occult progression or magical-site competition; Ashglass is not consumed by these spells.
why: The central fantasy promise cannot emerge from a damage/ward pair available to every culture.
solution: First close one original map-level magical loop: site discovery → resource and qualified practitioner commitment → visible strategic effect → rival warning and counteraction → permanent consequence. Extend caster progression, school/faction access, artifice and sacred/occult distinctions only through integrated slices.
acceptance: A generated campaign earns, casts and counters the first strategic working with real costs and AI participation; saves/replay preserve effects; battle feedback shows actual outcomes. Broader published magic scope remains required until explicitly revised, not satisfied by one demonstration.

issue: Production commitments cannot be cancelled or reprioritized
evidence: The queue accepts up to five FIFO orders and spends coin upfront; the canonical command union has queue but no production cancel/reorder. Campaign A queued buildings and troops but exposed no corrective queue action.
why: A mistaken order or sudden war cannot be answered by correcting production, an avoidable frustration in a strategy game.
solution: Specify refund/sunk-industry rules, implement canonical cancellation and reordering, then expose direct controls and clear net costs. Preserve land-work and travel cancellation as distinct operations.
acceptance: Reorder/cancel partial buildings, units and naval hulls through UI and replay; captured or invalidated queues cannot refund value twice or mint resources.

issue: Starvation, arrears and siege isolation barely harm established forces
evidence: Save-valid authored population200 town with food11 versus consumption800 stays population200 for ten turns. Unpaid heavy troops retain strength85, recover morale20→85 and fatigue60→0, and still move1. Siege supplies reduce militia morale, not the real garrison.
why: Economic warfare and overstretch lack reliable consequences; increasing upkeep alone does not create the intended risk.
solution: Choose telegraphed, recoverable famine, arrears and local supply effects on real population/formations. Add a matching forecast and AI sustainability policy. Avoid an invisible punitive attrition layer.
acceptance: Sustained deficits create bounded consequences, recovery works, isolation affects actual defenders, and neither player nor AI enters an unrecoverable bookkeeping softlock.

issue: Diplomacy is a paid truce system rather than strategic obligations
evidence: UI provides war and peace with one-way coin plus5–30 turns. Grievances/war age affect acceptance; detached trust-100/respect0 versus trust100/respect100 yields identical assessment. No alliances, clients/tribute, negotiated access or resource clauses exist.
why: A diplomatic strategy cannot organize a different kind of power or punish a common aggressor beyond bilateral war/truce.
solution: Add a bounded clause/obligation model starting with negotiated access, exchange and client/tribute relations, including breach, visibility and AI valuation. Only expose relationship meters that have real effects; scope internal politics to chosen faction/victory needs.
acceptance: Offers, obligations, expiry/breach and AI responses are visible, saved, replayable and strategically exploitable with counterplay—not simply new buttons.

issue: Tactical deployment follows creation IDs instead of player intent
evidence: Deployment sorts formation IDs lexicographically into five columns/four ranks. Army-wide Advance/Brace/Flank/Withdraw and real pike/mounted/missile rules exist, but no player formation arrangement uses those roles deliberately.
why: Composition decisions are partially undermined by arbitrary placement; the player cannot intentionally put a screen ahead of missiles.
solution: Add compact formation-slot/role deployment policy and preview, sensible role-aware defaults and matching AI placement. Integrate with the reserve policy from R03; do not rewrite into RTS control.
acceptance: The same composition can deliberately adopt distinct legal deployments whose consequences are readable and deterministic; reordering unrelated entity IDs cannot silently choose the player's tactical plan.

issue: Research lacks enough transformative late branches and comparison clarity
evidence: C74/C99 finish ten practical technologies by75/84; Epic all factions by146, far before808 ending. Navigation and land works are genuine unlocks, but most of the25 development nodes are additive effects. Research UI is a long card catalog.
why: Knowledge loses strategic purpose and progression stops changing what players can do.
solution: Add mutually informing unlock branches that change logistics, specialization, political or magical capabilities; retain genuine instant-purchase rules rather than pretending there is a research queue. Show downstream unlocks, alternative costs and turns-to-afford based on current yields.
acceptance: Late research creates counters or new plans, not another mandatory+1; multiple earned campaigns choose different branches and can explain the opportunity cost in the UI.

issue: The world lacks independent powers and consequential discovery/event content
evidence: No executable minor-power, landmark, quest or branching-event registries. Current ruins are razed towns. Campaign A's chosen route finds no interactive landmark/quest in30 turns; this is one sample, not an all-world claim.
why: Exploration finds terrain/resources and peer realms but few discoveries that create a story or redirect a strategy.
solution: Implement one independent actor/site/event loop with persistent choices and AI valuation; then author state-triggered regional conflicts and a bounded endgame escalation. Establish mechanics and consequential outcomes before multiplying templates.
acceptance: Discovery can alter ownership, obligation, capability or geography through player choice; consequences survive save/replay and appear in a fog-safe ongoing history.

issue: Onboarding teaches navigation but not a complete first strategic loop
evidence: Opening prompt explains founding; Map guide teaches movement/windows/hotkeys. No staged teaching of household work, economy, magic prerequisites, battle interpretation and victory planning appeared.
why: The game presents mechanical depth without ensuring a new player understands what to do or why.
solution: Build an optional, state-aware first-campaign sequence with small real actions, previews and an accessible glossary. Tolerate alternate action order, do not spend for the player, and allow permanent opt-out.
acceptance: External first-time users can found/work/build/scout/research/fight and state their victory objective without consulting source or remembering invisible requirements.

issue: No implemented audio layer supports the game
evidence: Production scan found no browser audio integration and no tracked audio files; no music/effects/ambience controls appeared in live settings. This is not claimed as an audio listening test.
why: Battle, discovery, construction and victory lack a core layer of consequential feedback and atmosphere.
solution: Create an original restrained sonic palette: music, biome/settlement ambience, UI, orders, combat, magic and milestone cues. Trigger from authoritative presentation facts; implement user-gesture activation, category volume/mute, saved settings and voice limits.
acceptance: Licensed/provenanced sound families function across supported browsers, never affect simulation, respect mute/reduced-sensory preferences and scale without a voice explosion.

issue: Waykeeper binding and four specialist art aliases obscure playable roles
evidence: All 545 approvals and current live catalog IDs are present; all common 24-culture kits and existing works/deposits are covered. The UI rejects unregistered character.waykeeper before reaching its published shared fallback, yielding Generic. Four strategic specialists alias scout, spearman or cavalry art; their battle sets already exist.
why: Paid characters visibly fall back despite available artwork; a crossbow, javelin, halberd or lance role should not be mistaken for another recruit. This is not a missing common culture kit.
solution: Repair shared Waykeeper fallback first with zero new images. Commission four deliberate shared strategic specialist pilots with exact current role bindings; scale to culture-qualified variants only after review. Preserve the existing culture kit and provenance.
acceptance: A paid Waykeeper in multiple cultures resolves a truthful shared image without a failed-load pawn; four specialist roles are visually distinct in recruitment/cards/map at native use size; binding, fog and deferred page budgets pass.
effortNote: S for the immediate zero-image binding repair; M for four shared specialist pilots.

issue: Battle silhouettes, biome cohesion and contextual presentation need focused refinement
evidence: All 13 battle sets contain genuine east/west action animation: 832 frames and 130 clips. Native foot-role bodies are thin and materially simpler than strategic culture sprites; desert/alpine originals differ markedly in value and scale from variants. The controlled 120-soldier field is sparse. These are quality/context findings, not absent motion or missing live terrain IDs.
why: Thousands of simulated soldiers do not feel like a premium battle if identities, contact, casualties and terrain are hard to read.
solution: Preserve existing weighted rigs and authentic clips. Refine guard/cavalry/transport silhouette/material pilots and five biome originals before scaling; review actual clip playback and world/battle context. Prototype native coast interfaces against current projection and restrained battlefield pieces without implying nonexistent cover mechanics. Full culture battle rigs are P3, not the repair.
acceptance: Native fit/detail views distinguish roles, attacks, casts, casualties and retreats; timing/holds/loops are actually reviewed. Terrain originals/variants read as the same region. Revised pixels pass source/native/runtime and measured atlas/frame budgets.

issue: Empire-scale comparison and ongoing history require too much modal navigation
evidence: From map, another town's orders take registry→entry→Show selected orders; available search/sort are not an economic dashboard. Turn26 journal shows eight recent events dominated by movements; realm-windows renders up to16 supplied events and promises full tome after victory.
why: Managing forty towns/armies requires remembering numbers and repeating navigation; meaningful consequences disappear behind routine events.
solution: Add sortable economic/military/character summaries with direct scoped actions and persistent selection; provide paginated fog-safe player history with filters, grouped movement, pins and locate links. Do not send the full archive in every observation.
acceptance: Two/ten/forty-town tasks have measured bounded click/scroll cost; old own decisions remain discoverable mid-campaign without exposing hidden enemy history.

issue: Passing scale kernels do not certify the supported browser/game workload
basis: QA and performance evidence with limits
evidence: Dedicated QA includes real large maps/armies/battles, but concurrent instrumented Node timings and software/headless browser results are not min-spec hardware certification. Normal full archives already exceed limits; browser compatibility and input/device coverage remain bounded.
why: A commercial scale promise must remain smooth, saveable and operable on a declared supported configuration, not merely complete a synthetic kernel.
solution: Publish a supported map/seat/battle/device matrix, run isolated target-GPU p50/p95/p99 frame and memory tests, distinguish soldier counts from formation/hull durability, and test long active effects/fog/save/history workloads. Wire measured budgets into release gates.
acceptance: Early/middle/late and massive-battle scenarios meet explicit frame/turn/memory/save budgets on min-spec and reference hardware, with reproducible scenarios and no hidden skipped maximum-mode coverage.

issue: Release verification does not yet protect long-campaign invariants and all supported configurations
evidence: Unchanged contact gate fails; full chronicle benchmarks expose invalid saves; gameplay/production smoke passing does not cover every accepted campaign boundary. Initial production-smoke attempt was an audit-config launch error (spawn /bin/sh ENOENT), corrected on rerun—not a product defect.
why: A green subset can coexist with campaign-loss defects; players need a trustworthy release candidate and recovery path.
solution: Make full named gates truthful: accepted-command save invariants, long multiseed campaigns, archive limits, supported migrations, production asset failure, quota recovery and browser/input matrices. Preserve failing fixtures and separate historical frozen-schema benchmarks from current evidence.
acceptance: Zero unresolved P0s and no unexplained named-gate failures; declared migration/browser coverage actually executed; release artifacts reproducible from a clean checkout with licenses and recovery instructions.

issue: Reload/import accumulates overlapping world-map controls
evidence: Independent dev and production public-UI lifecycle runs: one faction-overview-control initially, five after four loads, nine after four imports, reset to one on document reload. Canvas remains one and sampled attached listeners stay constant. Duplicate sibling keys are reported in dev.
why: Stale overlapping UI accumulates through routine save use; it is a real lifecycle defect, not demonstrated runaway WebGL/listener leakage.
solution: Use unique component-scoped sibling keys or deliberate keyed subtrees at main.tsx:713. Add repeated-load/import DOM-count and working-control assertions in dev and production; do not characterize this as a proven GPU/worker leak.
acceptance: Exactly one live control and one canvas after repeated same-size/cross-size replacements, responsive controls and stable listeners; no full page reload required.

issue: Characters and major milestones lack a distinct narrative/payoff layer
evidence: Named roles have actual XP/missions/wounds/death, but no authored biography/relationship/office system. First appointed Waykeeper has numeric suffix2. Founding, arcane unlock, appointment and victory are mainly status lines; the battle report requires opening Journal.
why: The game records consequences more reliably than it makes the player care about particular people and turning points.
solution: Add a bounded set of traits/relationships or office conflicts tied to actual campaign facts; disambiguate names without exposing serials. Tier feedback into routine/notable/major, with concise aftermath cards, event anchors and restrained audio/camera cues. Avoid repeated blocking celebrations.
acceptance: Players can identify why a veteran or conquered capital matters and trace that story midgame; milestone feedback reflects real facts and is skippable without losing information.

issue: Materials have few competing uses and weak strategic denial value
evidence: Eight real deposits feed14 advanced development nodes or fixed-price own-market sales. Cavalry does not require horses; heavy troops do not require iron; Ashglass does not pay for current spells. D sparse ends with zero material extraction for every faction.
why: Taking or trading a resource rarely changes an opponent's available strategy enough to justify a large resource catalog.
solution: Before expanding from8 toward the written40+ target, connect a few resources to substitutable equipment/recruitment, infrastructure or ritual choices with competing sinks and catch-up paths. Add genuine exchange only with diplomatic obligations and AI valuation ready.
acceptance: At least several distinct deposit types change plans and create contestable tradeoffs; denial has a counter-strategy, AI extracts when useful, and more resources are not counted as depth by themselves.
